question.:question/problem: Calculate the length of the altitude $CH$ of the $△\,ABC$, if $A(-1,-2,-2)$, $B(-3,-3,-2)$, $C(0,-4,-2).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Note that the length of the altitude $CH$ can be related to the area of $△\,ABC$ as follows:

$$
{A}_{△}=\frac{1}{2}CH\cdot AB
$$

So, to find $CH,$ we first find ${A}_{△}.$ To start, we find the vectors $\overset{\to }{AB}$ and $\overset{\to }{AC}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =(-3i-3j-2k)-(-i-2j-2k) \\  & =-2i-j \\  & =⟨-2,-1,0⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =(-4j-2k)-(-i-2j-2k) \\  & =i-2j \\  & =⟨1,-2,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB}\times \overset{\to }{AC} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -2 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}|k \\  & =((-1)\cdot 0-(-2)\cdot 0)i-((-2)\cdot 0-1\cdot 0)j+((-2)\cdot (-2)-1\cdot (-1))k \\  & =5k \\  & =⟨0,0,5⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of the parallelogram spanned by $\overset{\to }{AB}$ and $\overset{\to }{AC}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =|\overset{\to }{AB}\times \overset{\to }{AC}| \\  & =\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{5}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{25} \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

The area of the triangle is half of the area of the respective parallelogram. So, the area of $△\,ABC$ is

$$
{A}_{△}=\frac{1}{2}A=\frac{5}{2}=\frac{5}{2}.
$$

Let's also compute $AB$ since it appears in the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =|\overset{\to }{AB}| \\  & =\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{0}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{5} \\  & =\sqrt{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, using the formula ${A}_{△}=\frac{1}{2}CH\cdot AB,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{△} & =\frac{1}{2}CH\cdot AB \\ \frac{5}{2} & =\frac{1}{2}CH\cdot \sqrt{5} \\ 5 & =CH\cdot \sqrt{5} \\ CH & =\frac{5}{\sqrt{5}} \\ CH & =\sqrt{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Calculate the length of the altitude $CH$ of the $△\,ABC$, if $A(-1,-1,-2)$, $B(0,1,-2)$, $C(-2,-2,-2).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Note that the length of the altitude $CH$ can be related to the area of $△\,ABC$ as follows:

$$
{A}_{△}=\frac{1}{2}CH\cdot AB
$$

So, to find $CH,$ we first find ${A}_{△}.$ To start, we find the vectors $\overset{\to }{AB}$ and $\overset{\to }{AC}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =(j-2k)-(-i-j-2k) \\  & =i+2j \\  & =⟨1,2,0⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =(-2i-2j-2k)-(-i-j-2k) \\  & =-i-j \\  & =⟨-1,-1,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB}\times \overset{\to }{AC} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 2 & 0 \\ -1 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}|k \\  & =(2\cdot 0-(-1)\cdot 0)i-(1\cdot 0-(-1)\cdot 0)j+(1\cdot (-1)-(-1)\cdot 2)k \\  & =k \\  & =⟨0,0,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of the parallelogram spanned by $\overset{\to }{AB}$ and $\overset{\to }{AC}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =|\overset{\to }{AB}\times \overset{\to }{AC}| \\  & =\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

The area of the triangle is half of the area of the respective parallelogram. So, the area of $△\,ABC$ is

$$
{A}_{△}=\frac{1}{2}A=\frac{1}{2}=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Let's also compute $AB$ since it appears in the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =|\overset{\to }{AB}| \\  & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{0}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{5} \\  & =\sqrt{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, using the formula ${A}_{△}=\frac{1}{2}CH\cdot AB,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{△} & =\frac{1}{2}CH\cdot AB \\ \frac{1}{2} & =\frac{1}{2}CH\cdot \sqrt{5} \\ 1 & =CH\cdot \sqrt{5} \\ CH & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \\ CH & =\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Calculate the length of the altitude $CH$ of the $△\,ABC$, if $A(-2,-2,-1)$, $B(-4,-3,-1)$, $C(-1,-4,-3).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Note that the length of the altitude $CH$ can be related to the area of $△\,ABC$ as follows:

$$
{A}_{△}=\frac{1}{2}CH\cdot AB
$$

So, to find $CH,$ we first find ${A}_{△}.$ To start, we find the vectors $\overset{\to }{AB}$ and $\overset{\to }{AC}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =(-4i-3j-k)-(-2i-2j-k) \\  & =-2i-j \\  & =⟨-2,-1,0⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =(-i-4j-3k)-(-2i-2j-k) \\  & =i-2j-2k \\  & =⟨1,-2,-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB}\times \overset{\to }{AC} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -2 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & -2 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ -2 & -2\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}|k \\  & =((-1)\cdot (-2)-(-2)\cdot 0)i-((-2)\cdot (-2)-1\cdot 0)j+((-2)\cdot (-2)-1\cdot (-1))k \\  & =2i-4j+5k \\  & =⟨2,-4,5⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of the parallelogram spanned by $\overset{\to }{AB}$ and $\overset{\to }{AC}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =|\overset{\to }{AB}\times \overset{\to }{AC}| \\  & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-4)^{2}+{5}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{45} \\  & =3\sqrt{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

The area of the triangle is half of the area of the respective parallelogram. So, the area of $△\,ABC$ is

$$
{A}_{△}=\frac{1}{2}A=\frac{3\sqrt{5}}{2}=\frac{3\sqrt{5}}{2}.
$$

Let's also compute $AB$ since it appears in the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =|\overset{\to }{AB}| \\  & =\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{0}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{5} \\  & =\sqrt{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, using the formula ${A}_{△}=\frac{1}{2}CH\cdot AB,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{△} & =\frac{1}{2}CH\cdot AB \\ \frac{3\sqrt{5}}{2} & =\frac{1}{2}CH\cdot \sqrt{5} \\ 3\sqrt{5} & =CH\cdot \sqrt{5} \\ CH & =\frac{3\sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{5}} \\ CH & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Calculate the length of the altitude $CH$ of the $△\,ABC$, if $A(-1,-2,0)$, $B(0,0,0)$, $C(-2,-3,-2).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Note that the length of the altitude $CH$ can be related to the area of $△\,ABC$ as follows:

$$
{A}_{△}=\frac{1}{2}CH\cdot AB
$$

So, to find $CH,$ we first find ${A}_{△}.$ To start, we find the vectors $\overset{\to }{AB}$ and $\overset{\to }{AC}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =0-(-i-2j) \\  & =i+2j \\  & =⟨1,2,0⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =(-2i-3j-2k)-(-i-2j) \\  & =-i-j-2k \\  & =⟨-1,-1,-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB}\times \overset{\to }{AC} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 2 & 0 \\ -1 & -1 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}|k \\  & =(2\cdot (-2)-(-1)\cdot 0)i-(1\cdot (-2)-(-1)\cdot 0)j+(1\cdot (-1)-(-1)\cdot 2)k \\  & =-4i+2j+k \\  & =⟨-4,2,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of the parallelogram spanned by $\overset{\to }{AB}$ and $\overset{\to }{AC}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =|\overset{\to }{AB}\times \overset{\to }{AC}| \\  & =\sqrt{(-4)^{2}+{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{21} \\  & =\sqrt{21}.\end{aligned}
$$

The area of the triangle is half of the area of the respective parallelogram. So, the area of $△\,ABC$ is

$$
{A}_{△}=\frac{1}{2}A=\frac{\sqrt{21}}{2}=\frac{\sqrt{21}}{2}.
$$

Let's also compute $AB$ since it appears in the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =|\overset{\to }{AB}| \\  & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{0}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{5} \\  & =\sqrt{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, using the formula ${A}_{△}=\frac{1}{2}CH\cdot AB,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{△} & =\frac{1}{2}CH\cdot AB \\ \frac{\sqrt{21}}{2} & =\frac{1}{2}CH\cdot \sqrt{5} \\ \sqrt{21} & =CH\cdot \sqrt{5} \\ CH & =\frac{\sqrt{21}}{\sqrt{5}} \\ CH & =\frac{\sqrt{105}}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Calculate the length of the altitude $CH$ of the $△\,ABC$, if $A(-2,-1,-1)$, $B(-4,0,1)$, $C(-5,-3,-6).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Note that the length of the altitude $CH$ can be related to the area of $△\,ABC$ as follows:

$$
{A}_{△}=\frac{1}{2}CH\cdot AB
$$

So, to find $CH,$ we first find ${A}_{△}.$ To start, we find the vectors $\overset{\to }{AB}$ and $\overset{\to }{AC}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =(-4i+k)-(-2i-j-k) \\  & =-2i+j+2k \\  & =⟨-2,1,2⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =(-5i-3j-6k)-(-2i-j-k) \\  & =-3i-2j-5k \\  & =⟨-3,-2,-5⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB}\times \overset{\to }{AC} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -2 & 1 & 2 \\ -3 & -2 & -5\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -2 & -5\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 \\ -3 & -5\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ -3 & -2\end{aligned}|k \\  & =(1\cdot (-5)-(-2)\cdot 2)i-((-2)\cdot (-5)-(-3)\cdot 2)j+((-2)\cdot (-2)-(-3)\cdot 1)k \\  & =-i-16j+7k \\  & =⟨-1,-16,7⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of the parallelogram spanned by $\overset{\to }{AB}$ and $\overset{\to }{AC}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =|\overset{\to }{AB}\times \overset{\to }{AC}| \\  & =\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+(-16)^{2}+{7}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{306} \\  & =3\sqrt{34}.\end{aligned}
$$

The area of the triangle is half of the area of the respective parallelogram. So, the area of $△\,ABC$ is

$$
{A}_{△}=\frac{1}{2}A=\frac{3\sqrt{34}}{2}=\frac{3\sqrt{34}}{2}.
$$

Let's also compute $AB$ since it appears in the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =|\overset{\to }{AB}| \\  & =\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+{1}^{2}+{2}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, using the formula ${A}_{△}=\frac{1}{2}CH\cdot AB,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{△} & =\frac{1}{2}CH\cdot AB \\ \frac{3\sqrt{34}}{2} & =\frac{1}{2}CH\cdot 3 \\ \sqrt{34} & =CH\cdot 1 \\ CH & =\frac{\sqrt{34}}{1} \\ CH & =\sqrt{34}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Calculate the length of the altitude $CH$ of the $△\,ABC$, if $A(-2,0,2)$, $B(1,5,3)$, $C(-3,-3,-1).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Note that the length of the altitude $CH$ can be related to the area of $△\,ABC$ as follows:

$$
{A}_{△}=\frac{1}{2}CH\cdot AB
$$

So, to find $CH,$ we first find ${A}_{△}.$ To start, we find the vectors $\overset{\to }{AB}$ and $\overset{\to }{AC}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =(i+5j+3k)-(-2i+2k) \\  & =3i+5j+k \\  & =⟨3,5,1⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =(-3i-3j-k)-(-2i+2k) \\  & =-i-3j-3k \\  & =⟨-1,-3,-3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB}\times \overset{\to }{AC} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 3 & 5 & 1 \\ -1 & -3 & -3\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}5 & 1 \\ -3 & -3\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ -1 & -3\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}3 & 5 \\ -1 & -3\end{aligned}|k \\  & =(5\cdot (-3)-(-3)\cdot 1)i-(3\cdot (-3)-(-1)\cdot 1)j+(3\cdot (-3)-(-1)\cdot 5)k \\  & =-12i+8j-4k \\  & =⟨-12,8,-4⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of the parallelogram spanned by $\overset{\to }{AB}$ and $\overset{\to }{AC}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =|\overset{\to }{AB}\times \overset{\to }{AC}| \\  & =\sqrt{(-12)^{2}+{8}^{2}+(-4)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{224} \\  & =4\sqrt{14}.\end{aligned}
$$

The area of the triangle is half of the area of the respective parallelogram. So, the area of $△\,ABC$ is

$$
{A}_{△}=\frac{1}{2}A=\frac{4\sqrt{14}}{2}=2\sqrt{14}.
$$

Let's also compute $AB$ since it appears in the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =|\overset{\to }{AB}| \\  & =\sqrt{{3}^{2}+{5}^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{35} \\  & =\sqrt{35}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, using the formula ${A}_{△}=\frac{1}{2}CH\cdot AB,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{△} & =\frac{1}{2}CH\cdot AB \\ 2\sqrt{14} & =\frac{1}{2}CH\cdot \sqrt{35} \\ 4\sqrt{14} & =CH\cdot \sqrt{35} \\ CH & =\frac{4\sqrt{14}}{\sqrt{35}} \\ CH & =\frac{4\sqrt{10}}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
